topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestFollowSource_HeadsDivergeThenConverge`
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Job:** `memory-all-opn-op-geth`

**CI run:** https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/121197/workflows/129b5275-5553-4898-96f6-8d86c6cc9afc/jobs/4696329/tests

**Branch:** develop

**Date:** 2026-03-30

## Error

Panic during test teardown — `pebble: closed` race condition in SafeDB:

```
panic: pebble: closed

goroutine 38932 [running]:
github.com/cockroachdb/pebble.(*DB).newIter(...)
	/home/circleci/go/pkg/mod/github.com/cockroachdb/pebble@v1.1.5/db.go:1011 +0x585
github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-node/node/safedb.(*SafeDB).SafeHeadAtL1(...)
	/home/circleci/project/op-node/node/safedb/safedb.go:170 +0x1eb
github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-supernode/supernode/chain_container/virtual_node.(*simpleVirtualNode).L1AtSafeHead(...)
	/home/circleci/project/op-supernode/supernode/chain_container/virtual_node/virtual_node.go:240 +0x184
github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-supernode/supernode/chain_container.(*simpleChainContainer).safeDBAtL2(...)
	/home/circleci/project/op-supernode/supernode/chain_container/chain_container.go:403 +0x269
github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-supernode/supernode/chain_container.(*simpleChainContainer).OptimisticAt(...)
	/home/circleci/project/op-supernode/supernode/chain_container/chain_container.go:450 +0x26b
github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop.(*Interop).l1Inclusion(...)
	/home/circleci/project/op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/algo.go:41 +0x116
```

## Analysis

The interop activity goroutine calls `SafeHeadAtL1` on a pebble DB that has already been closed during shutdown. This is a use-after-close race — the supernode's interop activity is still running when the SafeDB is closed during teardown.

The fix likely needs to ensure the interop activity is fully stopped before closing the SafeDB, or add a closed-state check in `SafeHeadAtL1`.

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestSuperCannonRootBeyondProposedBlock_ValidRoot/mt-cannon-next`
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Reporting a pre-existing test failure.

**Test:** `TestSuperCannonRootBeyondProposedBlock_ValidRoot/mt-cannon-next`
**Package:** `op-e2e/faultproofs`
**CI run:** https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19791 (encountered during ethereum-optimism/optimism#19791)

## Failure

The test times out waiting for the game to resolve to "Defender Won". The challenger completes all moves (including the final step), but the game remains "In Progress" indefinitely.

The interop recipe sets `DisputeMaxClockDuration: 302400` (3.5 days / 84 hours). After `AdvanceTime(MaxClockDuration)`, the game's resolve calls succeed (transactions published) but the game never transitions to "Defender Won".

## Reproduction

Reproduced locally on both game type 4 (SUPER_CANNON, original develop) and game type 9 (SUPER_CANNON_KONA), confirming this is pre-existing and not related to the game type change.

```
OP_E2E_CANNON_ENABLED=true go test -count=1 -timeout 30m \
  -run 'TestSuperCannonRootBeyondProposedBlock_ValidRoot/mt-cannon-next' \
  -v ./op-e2e/faultproofs
```

## Key log observations

- Challenger logs: `Game info ... claims=74 status="In Progress"` (never changes)
- `resolve claim` transactions are published successfully every ~6s
- `eth_call` for resolve returns `ClockNotExpired` (`0x9a076646`) — normal pre-check behavior
- `MaxClockDuration` reported by the game contract: 84h0m0s (302400 seconds)
- The test uses `WithNextVMOnly` so only runs on `mt-cannon-next`

topIssues.title: Design doc for shared dispute game
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19253 provides the upgrade to SuperDisputeGame but each chain has it's own. Next we need the ability to merge chains into a shared SuperDisputeGame. This issue is for creating a design doc.

Let's keep this lightweight. `OPCM.migrate()` was already implemented, we can just AI-generate a design doc from this as a starting point and use it to discuss the changes for OPCM v2, and any tradeoffs like (hopefully not) resetting withdrawals, and the need for pre-approved hardcoded super roots.

topIssues.title: kona: MessageGraph uses hardcoded MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW instead of dependency set config
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Description

Kona's `MessageGraph` in `rust/kona/crates/protocol/interop/src/graph.rs` (line ~180) uses a hardcoded `MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW` constant (7 days) when checking message expiry. It does not read the configurable message expiry window from the dependency set.

This means the fault proof program (kona) cannot detect expired messages when the dependency set has a custom (shorter) expiry window configured, even though the supernode and challenger trace provider correctly use the dependency set's value.

## Impact

The `TestInteropFaultProofs_MessageExpiry` acceptance test cannot run its FPP subtests because the test configures a 10-second expiry window via `WithMessageExpiryWindow(10)`, but kona still uses the 7-day hardcoded constant and doesn't detect the expiry.

## Expected behavior

Kona should read the message expiry window from the dependency set configuration (passed via rollup configs or the preimage oracle) rather than using a hardcoded constant.

## References

- Hardcoded constant: `rust/kona/crates/protocol/interop/src/graph.rs` ~line 180
- Acceptance test skip: `op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go` in `RunMessageExpiryTest`

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth): Drop interop transactions after reorg
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
**Description**

This PR adds a wrapper type `OpPool` around reth's `Pool` type that allows overriding specific behaviors.

In particular, the code snippet that we're overriding here is the following: https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/930f2a6eb257854138bb9e291c7013586fcd0223/crates/transaction-pool/src/maintain.rs#L412-L431

Inside `maintain_transaction_pool`, after handling a Reorg, the node reinjects the dropped transactions back into the transaction pool. When interop is enabled, this can lead to an infinite loop that prevents the chain from recovering, since if the dropped transactions are the interop transactions that caused the reorg in the first place, the node never recovers and keeps trying to re-add the invalid transactions back to a new block.

The problem: `pool.add_external_transactions` by itself does not allow us to know when a reorg has happened. For this we have `pool.on_canonical_state_change`, which tells us when a reorg has happened but not which transactions were dropped from the old chain.

Additionally, because `pool.add_external_transactions` is an async function, it's possible (even if extremely unlikely) that between the two function calls, some other task is scheduled to run and calls `pool.add_external_transactions` before the `maintain_transaction_pool` task can do it. If we only filtered once, this could lead to a scenario where the interop transactions don't get filtered after a reorg and lead to more reorgs.

This PR does the following:
1. When `pool.on_canonical_state_change` is called with a `PoolUpdateKind::Reorg` argument, we set a flag in the pool's state that a reorg has happened, and record the current time
2. Inside `pool.add_external_transactions`, if the flag is active, we filter out interop transactions (see `is_interop_tx`)
3. After filtering, clear the flag
4. If the flag was not set, but we're within `REORG_WINDOW` seconds since the last reorg happened, filter the transactions anyway

This ensures that:
- Even if the `pool.add_external_transactions` task ends up getting delayed and scheduled after `REORG_WINDOW` seconds, we will still filter it at least once: from the code, we **know** that there will be a call to it afterwards that we need to filter, at least
- If other tasks race the maintenance task and clear the flag, but then the task gets scheduled within `REORG_WINDOW`, the interop transactions being reinjected are filtered correctly anyway and we have no issues

The only remaining scenario where the filter wouldn't work is: a reorg happens, some other tokio task calls `add_external_transactions` without interop transactions to clear the filter flag, then `REORG_WINDOW` seconds pass before the original maintenance task calls `add_external_transactions`.

In this PR, I've set `REORG_WINDOW` to 30 seconds. This value is pretty high in comparison to the block times, and we could definitely set it much lower without much issues. I've chosen a higher value to be on the safe side.

Dropping the interop transactions like this is safe because the relayer can re-submit them after the reorg has settled.

The filter is enabled on op-reth startup by checking if interop is enabled in the chain config. This check is only done once, so a change from interop disabled to interop enabled is not handled by this PR.

**Tests**

Tests added to `pool.rs` and unskip `TestSupernodeInteropInvalidMessageReplacement` which now passes correctly with op-reth

**Additional context**

See also #19411

**Metadata**

- Fixes #19567
- Supersedes #19642 (this approach vendors the entire `maintain_transaction_pool` logic into op-reth to add the filter in-line, but this creates too much maintenance burden)

**Future work**

Ideally, reth's trait infrastructure would enable us to set an arbitrary transaction filter at different spots inside `maintain_task` so we could achieve this without potential race conditions and without needing to duplicate logic. Alternatively, we could modify some of the existing functions to pass more information to the pool functions so we could get rid of the `REORG_WINDOW` fallback.

Additionally, the existing `supervisor_client` filter located in op-reth's [`maintain_transaction_pool_interop`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/7c57cf9837850bc94625f73f5fee93cfcad58da2/rust/op-reth/crates/txpool/src/maintain.rs#L153) should probably be adapted to run via the `OpPool` type when `add_external_transactions`, `add_transaction`, `add_transactions`, `add_transactions_with_origins`, `add_transaction_and_subscribe` (etc) run instead. This would mean the pool can filter transactions out *before* they even get added to the pool in the first place.

topPRs.title: fix(kona): use configurable message expiry window in MessageGraph
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Add `message_expiry_window: u64` parameter to `MessageGraph::derive()` instead of using hardcoded `MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW` constant
- Load `DependencySet` from preimage oracle local key 8 in `BootInfo`
- Thread expiry window from `BootInfo` through `SuperchainConsolidator` to `MessageGraph`
- Add tests verifying custom expiry window behavior (expired and within-window cases)

## Motivation

`MessageGraph::check_single_dependency()` was using the hardcoded `MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW` constant (7 days) instead of the configurable value from the `DependencySet`. The Go FPP host already serves a `DependencySet` (with configurable `overrideMessageExpiryWindow`) via the preimage oracle at local key 8, but Kona's `BootInfo` didn't load it. This prevented acceptance tests that configure custom expiry windows (e.g., `TestInteropFaultProofs_MessageExpiry`) from working correctly with Kona's fault proof program.

Closes #19636

## Test plan

- [x] All 11 existing `MessageGraph` tests updated to pass `MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW` explicitly — behavior identical to before
- [x] New test `test_derive_and_resolve_graph_message_expired_custom_window` — proves custom 10s window triggers expiry
- [x] New test `test_derive_and_resolve_graph_message_not_expired_within_custom_window` — proves boundary correctness
- [x] `cargo test --package kona-interop --all-features` — 31 tests pass
- [x] `cargo test --package kona-proof-interop` — 30 tests pass
- [x] Default behavior preserved: `DependencySet::get_message_expiry_window()` falls back to `MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW` when no override is set

topPRs.title: refactor(contracts): separate v4/v5 init slot clearing in L2ContractsManagerUtils
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
## Summary
- Separate the interleaved v4/v5 initialization slot clearing into distinct code blocks — v4 path is fully contained in an `if (_slot != v5Slot)` block, v5 path runs unconditionally below
- Add `L2ContractsManager_InvalidV5Offset` revert when v5 slot is passed with a non-zero offset
- Add tests for non-zero `_offset` (previously untested) and the new v5 offset validation
- Bump L2ContractsManager to 1.3.0

## Motivation
The previous code always ran both v4 and v5 clearing logic, relying on implicit no-ops for the version that doesn't apply. When `_slot == v5Slot`, this caused a redundant SSTORE and a confusing re-read of a slot that was just written to. The refactored version is semantically identical but easier to reason about.

## Test plan
- [x] All 9 `L2ContractsManagerUtils_UpgradeToAndCall_Test` tests pass
- [x] New: `test_upgrade_v4NonZeroOffset_succeeds` — exercises offset=2 bit-shifting
- [x] New: `test_upgrade_v4InitializingNonZeroOffset_reverts` — revert with offset=2
- [x] New: `test_upgrade_v5InvalidOffset_reverts` — validates new offset guard

topPRs.title: fix(deployer): isolate anvil FOUNDRY_HOME to prevent ~/.foundry bloat
topPRs.author: JosepBove
topPRs.body:
Anvil writes chain state to ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/ by default, and Stop() only kills the process without cleaning up these files. Over time this causes ~/.foundry to grow to 100+ GB.

Fix by setting FOUNDRY_HOME to an isolated temp directory per anvil instance, which is cleaned up when Stop() is called. A WithFoundryHome option is also exposed for callers that want to manage the directory lifecycle themselves.
